brief: brief-hwaccel-direction.md (the owner's question of 2026-11-21: keep one spare worker and scale when it is taken, in place of scaling once encoding falls behind) and brief-js162.md: jellyscale_transcode_queue_cores read 0 at the one snapshot of every run, 300 seconds in, every stalling run included; no refused play was among the runs. Cost named in the brief: one idle worker's reservation, on nodes that are mostly reserved (one at 94% of its CPU).
tradeoff: An idle worker's reservation at all times, paid by every deployment that turns the example autoscaler on, against the viewer who triggers a scale-up waiting, stalling or being refused while a worker starts.
entry: The scaling signal is spare room as well as falling behind, spare room first. JS-164's second gauge becomes the dearest job a new viewer would be admitted for now, for the whole cluster in reference cores, by JS-161's rule: cores held by a helper of a watched job its own worker does not hold at 1.2 times real time alone are not free, cores of any other helper are; JS-164 depends on JS-161 and its example scaling query is on that gauge, its example alert on the demand number. JS-057's example keeps room for one more job of a size the operator states (the example: the dearest re-encode in the table) and adds a worker when the room falls below it; falling behind and refusals stay as the backstop and the readable reason, and are measured with the target at zero. docs/running.md states the cost and how to set the target to zero. No new task. JS-164's first criterion stands: the queue signal is measured at 0 during a stall once per run, and unobserved for a refused play. BL-243 stays. Given up: one worker's reservation idle, by operators who turn the example on; a cluster with no room for it has only the backstop. Rejected: spare room alone (a cluster that cannot keep the room would have no signal and no reason to read); falling behind alone (the triggering viewer pays the worker's start). Unverified when decided: the time from a pod's creation to its first job (JS-166 measures it); how often the dogfood would sit below the target. Data that reopens it: JS-166 and JS-057 measuring demand-to-ready under about 10 seconds, with BL-243's hold, would make spare room optional in the example; JS-057's 14 days showing the room below target most of the time on fixed nodes.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'The cluster can grow and shrink with demand by itself.' Goal 1 over goal 5: 'Playback never surprises a viewer' ahead of 'Operating it stays boring'. 'when the cluster needed more workers they can see what demanded them'.
